searchDocs.title: connect​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> EventSwitchboard:connect( port: string, callback: ( player: Player , T... ) → () ) → () → () Sets the callback for port. Errors if the port already has one. Returns a function that removes it.

searchDocs.title: fireServer​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> EventSwitchboard:fireServer( port: string, ...: T... ) → () Sends the arguments to the server callback for port.

searchDocs.title: fireServerPredicted​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> EventSwitchboard:fireServerPredicted( predictions: {Prediction}, port: string, ...: T... ) → () Sends the arguments to the server callback for port, and shows predictions on their replicators until the server has handled this call. Build each prediction with a replicator's prediction method. The server must make this call's replicator changes before its handler returns. SeeClient prediction.

searchDocs.title: rateLimit​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> EventSwitchboard:rateLimit(limit: Limit) → EventSwitchboard Sets the rate limit for calls to each port from each player, replacing the default of 60 at once and 30 per second. Returns the same switchboard, so it can be chained where it's created. Errors if the limit is invalid. shopSwitchboard = Sencha.eventSwitchboard(gt.number()):rateLimit({ burst = 5, perSecond = 2 }),

searchDocs.content: </> EventSwitchboard:destroy() → () Destroys the remote instance on the server.

searchDocs.title: replicator​
searchDocs.content: </> SavedSource:replicator( valueType: GreenTeaType, lookup: (savedData: D) → T, incrementalConfig: SavedIncrementalConfig<T,P>? ) → SavedReplicator<D,T,P> Creates a SavedReplicator for the part of the saved data that lookup returns. The saved data passed to lookup is fully typed from the source's GreenTea type. researchReplicator = PlayerDataSource:replicator(gt.array(gt.string()), function(playerData) return playerData.research end), lookup must return an existing table from the saved data, or a primitive, and must not yield. Changes are found by comparing what it returns, so a lookup that builds a new table counts as changed on every save.

searchDocs.title: setFetchFunction​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> SavedSource:setFetchFunction(fetchAsync: (player: Player ) → D?) → () Sets the function that returns a player's saved data, yielding until it has loaded, or nil if it never loads. Replicators from this source wait for it to be set. PlayerDataSource:setFetchFunction(function(player) local didLoad, playerData = PlayerDataServer.waitForPlayerData(player) return if didLoad then playerData else nil end)

searchDocs.title: replicateChanges​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> SavedSource:replicateChanges( player: Player , newData: D, oldData: D? ) → () Tells the source that a player's saved data changed, including when it first loads (oldData is nil). Each replicator whose part changed sends it to the player, then fires its onChanged. Call this from your store's change callback. PlayerDataSource:replicateChanges(player, newData, oldData)

searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client This is a yielding function. Yields </> FunctionSwitchboard:invokeServer( port: string, ...: T... ) → R... Calls the server callback for port and returns what it returns.

searchDocs.title: get​
searchDocs.content: </> TemporaryPlayerReplicator:get( player: Player? -- required on the server, left out on the client ) → T Returns the current value without yielding. On the client, errors if the value hasn't arrived yet. Call Sencha.waitForReplicators while loading, or use TemporaryPlayerReplicator:getAsync or TemporaryPlayerReplicator:observe in code that may run earlier. On the client, this includes pending predictions. TemporaryPlayerReplicator:getConfirmed returns the server's value without them.

searchDocs.title: getAsync​
searchDocs.content: This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> TemporaryPlayerReplicator:getAsync( player: Player? -- required on the server, left out on the client ) → T Returns the current value, yielding until it's available. Server values always exist, so this only yields on the client. On the client, this includes pending predictions. TemporaryPlayerReplicator:getConfirmed returns the server's value without them.

searchDocs.title: set​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> TemporaryPlayerReplicator:set( player: Player , value: T ) → () Sets a player's value and sends it to them. Errors if the value doesn't match the replicator's type. Setting a primitive to the value it already has does nothing; setting a table always counts as a change.

searchDocs.title: tryUpdate​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> TemporaryPlayerReplicator:tryUpdate( player: Player , callback: (value: T) → ( boolean, T? ) ) → boolean Calls callback with a player's current value. If it returns true and a new value, the value is set as with TemporaryPlayerReplicator:set; if it returns false, nothing changes. Returns what callback returned first. callback must not yield, so nothing else can change the value between reading and setting it. local didBuy = CurrencyNetwork.coinsReplicator:tryUpdate(player, function(coins) if coins < 10 then return false end return true, coins - 10 end)

searchDocs.title: applyIncrementalUpdate​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> TemporaryPlayerReplicator:applyIncrementalUpdate( player: Player , patch: P ) → () Applies patch to a player's value with the incremental config's apply, then sends only the patch to them. Errors if the patch or the new value doesn't match its type, or if the replicator has no incremental config. An empty table patch does nothing.

searchDocs.title: onChanged​
searchDocs.content: </> TemporaryPlayerReplicator:onChanged(callback: ( player: Player , newValue: T, oldValue: T ) → ()) → Disconnect Calls callback when the value changes, not for the initial value. On the server this fires for any player whose value changes; on the client player is always the local player. On the server, the change is sent to clients before callback runs, so anything it changes in response reaches clients after the change that caused it. On the client, this also fires when a prediction is made, and again if it's rolled back. UseTemporaryPlayerReplicator:onConfirmedChanged to only hear about the server's changes.

searchDocs.title: observe​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> TemporaryPlayerReplicator:observe(callback: ( newValue: T, oldValue: T? ) → ()) → Disconnect Calls callback with the current value right away if it has arrived (otherwise when it arrives), then on every change. oldValue is the value before the change, or nil for the first call. CurrencyNetwork.coinsReplicator:observe(function(coins, oldCoins) print(`coins: {oldCoins} -> {coins}`) -- oldCoins is nil the first time end) This includes predictions: it fires when a prediction is made, and again if it's rolled back.

searchDocs.title: onUpdateReceived​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> TemporaryPlayerReplicator:onUpdateReceived(callback: ( newValue: T, oldValue: T, patch: P ) → ()) → Disconnect Calls callback for each patch received, after the value is updated. Only replicators with an incremental config receive patches; calling this on one without errors. Whole values (the first value, or a set) don't fire this; use TemporaryPlayerReplicator:onChanged to see every change. Patches always come from the server: predictions don't fire this, and newValue and oldValue are the server's values.

searchDocs.title: getObservable​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> TemporaryPlayerReplicator:getObservable() → ObservableValue<T> Returns an ObservableValue that follows the replicated value, for code that works with ObservableValues, like the ReactObservableValue hooks. Calling this again returns the same one. Setting it doesn't change the replicated value. Errors if the value hasn't arrived yet. local coins = ReactObservableValue.useObservableValue(CurrencyNetwork.coinsReplicator:getObservable()) The observable includes pending predictions, like TemporaryPlayerReplicator:get.

searchDocs.title: getConfirmed​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> TemporaryPlayerReplicator:getConfirmed() → T Returns the value the server sent, without any pending predictions. TemporaryPlayerReplicator:get returns the predicted value while a prediction is pending; use this when code must only act on what the server has confirmed. Errors if the value hasn't arrived yet.

searchDocs.title: onConfirmedChanged​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> TemporaryPlayerReplicator:onConfirmedChanged(callback: ( player: Player , newValue: T, oldValue: T ) → ()) → Disconnect Calls callback when the server's value changes, not for predictions or the initial value. player is always the local player. TemporaryPlayerReplicator:onChanged also fires for predictions, and again if a wrong prediction is rolled back. Use this instead for effects that should only change for confirmed values: CurrencyNetwork.coinsReplicator:onConfirmedChanged(function(_player, coins, oldCoins) if coins > oldCoins then playCoinsGainedSound() -- never plays for a prediction that gets rolled back end end)

searchDocs.title: prediction​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> TemporaryPlayerReplicator:prediction(predict: ((value: T) → T) | P) → Prediction Builds a prediction for this replicator. The returned prediction can be used with a predicted remote call such asinvokeServerPredicted or fireServerPredicted. While the call is pending, TemporaryPlayerReplicator:get, TemporaryPlayerReplicator:observe and TemporaryPlayerReplicator:onChanged show the value with the prediction applied; it's removed when the server confirms the call. predict is either a function that returns the predicted value, or a patch on a replicator with an incremental config. A patch is applied with the config's apply, the same way the server's patches are. CurrencyNetwork.buyItemRemote:invokeServerPredicted({ CurrencyNetwork.coinsReplicator:prediction(function(coins) return coins - 10 end), }, "sword")

searchDocs.title: Disconnect​
searchDocs.content: </> type Disconnect = () → () Every listener method returns a Disconnect, the cleanup function. Call it to stop listening. It's safe to call more than once, and can be handed to a cleanup library or returned from a React effect.

searchDocs.title: Prediction​
searchDocs.content: </> type Prediction = { channel: any, predict: any } A prediction for one replicator, built with that replicator's prediction method and passed to a predicted remote call such as invokeServerPredicted or fireServerPredicted. channel is typed any to work around a limitation in Luau's older type checker. Predictions are still type-checked when you create them. Each replicator's prediction method checks its function or patch against that replicator's value type.

searchDocs.title: Limit​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Limit { burst: number-- calls a player can make at once; at least 1 perSecond: number-- calls a player gets back each second; more than 0 } A rate limit for calls from clients, passed to :rateLimit(...) on any remote. Each player has their own budget.

searchDocs.title: unreliableEvent​
searchDocs.content: </> Sencha.unreliableEvent( ...: GreenTeaType-- the type of each argument ) → Event<T...> Creates an Event backed by an UnreliableRemoteEvent. It has the same API as Sencha.event, but messages may be dropped or arrive out of order, and payloads are limited to roughly 900 bytes. Use it for repeating updates where only the latest matters, never for messages that must arrive.

searchDocs.title: func​
searchDocs.content: </> Sencha.func( args: GreenTeaArgs,-- gt.args(...) returns: GreenTeaReturns-- gt.returns(...) ) → Function<T...,R...> Creates a Function, a typed RemoteFunction the client invokes on the server. buyItemRemote = Sencha.func(gt.args(gt.string()), gt.returns(gt.boolean())),

searchDocs.title: eventSwitchboard​
searchDocs.content: </> Sencha.eventSwitchboard( ...: GreenTeaType-- the type of each argument after the port ) → EventSwitchboard<T...> Creates an [EventSwitchboard]: one RemoteEvent that routes client calls to a server callback by port name.

searchDocs.title: funcSwitchboard​
searchDocs.content: </> Sencha.funcSwitchboard( args: GreenTeaArgs,-- gt.args(...) returns: GreenTeaReturns-- gt.returns(...) ) → FunctionSwitchboard<T...,R...> Creates a [FunctionSwitchboard]: one RemoteFunction that routes client calls to a server callback by port name.

searchDocs.title: savedSource​
searchDocs.content: </> Sencha.savedSource( name: string,-- a name unique to this store savedDataType: GreenTeaType-- the built GreenTea type of the saved data ) → SavedSource<D> Creates a SavedSource for one store of saved player data. Create one per store in a shared module, then create replicators from it with SavedSource:replicator. -- ReplicatedStorage/PlayerDataSource.luau return Sencha.savedSource("PlayerData", PlayerDataTypes.PlayerData)

searchDocs.title: define​
searchDocs.content: </> Sencha.define( parent: Instance ,-- usually script implementations: T-- a table of remotes and replicators ) → T Names and sets up every remote and replicator in implementations from its key, and returns the same table. Remotes are created under parent, and each replicator's name is parent:GetFullName() plus its key, so the same module resolves to the same remotes and replicators on both sides. Each remote and replicator can only be defined once.

searchDocs.title: waitForReplicators​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> Sencha.waitForReplicators() → () Yields until every replicator the server has defined has its first value on this client, including ones whose modules the client hasn't required yet. After this returns, get() is safe on every replicator. Call this once while loading, before starting systems that read replicated values. If this is still waiting after 5 seconds, a warning lists the replicators that don't have a value yet.

searchDocs.title: fireServer​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> Event:fireServer(...: T...) → () Sends the arguments to the server.

searchDocs.title: fireServerPredicted​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> Event:fireServerPredicted( predictions: {Prediction}, ...: T... ) → () Sends the arguments to the server, and shows predictions on their replicators until the server has handled this call. Build each prediction with a replicator's prediction method. Unreliable events can't be predicted. The server must make this call's replicator changes before its handler returns. SeeClient prediction.

searchDocs.title: fireClient​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> Event:fireClient( player: Player , ...: T... ) → () Sends the arguments to one player.

searchDocs.title: fireAllClients​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> Event:fireAllClients(...: T...) → () Sends the arguments to every player.

searchDocs.title: onClientEvent​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> Event:onClientEvent(callback: (T...) → ()) → Disconnect Calls callback whenever the server fires this event to this client.

searchDocs.title: onServerEvent​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> Event:onServerEvent(callback: ( player: Player , T... ) → ()) → Disconnect Calls callback whenever a client fires this event, after the call passes the rate limit and type check. Each call spends one token and is checked once, however many listeners there are.

searchDocs.title: rateLimit​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> Event:rateLimit(limit: Limit) → Event Sets the rate limit for calls from each player, replacing the default of 60 at once and 30 per second. Returns the same event, so it can be chained where it's created. Errors if the limit is invalid. exportItemRemote = Sencha.event(gt.string()):rateLimit({ burst = 10, perSecond = 4 }),

searchDocs.title: destroy​
searchDocs.content: </> Event:destroy() → () Disconnects every listener and, on the server, destroys the remote instance.
